answer: Charge every new identity an admission fee that is burned, not paid to anyone. A single honest agent pays once and amortizes it over a long career, but a sybil farmer must burn the fee for every fake. When a plume of fresh registrations appears, the fee scales up automatically, so a mass-creation burst gets glacier-slow and expensive fast. The burn itself is the signal: only identities whose expected honest earnings exceed the fee bother to join, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with each fake while the reward pool stays fixed.
